title: RFC 9110: HTTP Semantics
supports: HTTP method, created-resource, Location, redirect and error semantics; the caller-key replay window, product limits and uniform expiry/takedown 404 policy are chosen workshop rules.

title: RFC 3986: URI Generic Syntax
supports: URI scheme and authority components and security considerations; the HTTP(S)-only validation policy is an explicit workshop design choice, not a safety guarantee.

title: RFC 9111: HTTP Caching
supports: Conforming HTTP caches must not store or reuse a response carrying no-store; this does not synchronize an application cache or guarantee privacy against hostile clients.

title: A Proof for the Queuing Formula: L = λW
author: John D. C. Little
relevantSections: Public abstract: finite means and stationary-process conditions
supports: A relationship between average number in the system, arrival rate, and mean total time, under the stated theorem conditions; it does not give a worker count or burst bound.

title: PERF05-BP04 Load test your workload
supports: Testing the entire workload under realistic conditions, with defined objectives, monitored metrics, and expected and larger loads.

title: RFC 6585: Additional HTTP Status Codes
supports: 429 denotes rate limiting and can carry Retry-After; caller identification, enforcement scope and limit values are separate design choices.

title: PostgreSQL 16: Constraints
relevantSections: 5.4.3–5.4.5: unique constraints, primary keys, foreign keys
supports: Unique/compound keys, primary-key indexes and referential integrity; immutable ownership and permanent reservation retention are separate workshop rules.

title: PostgreSQL 16: INSERT
supports: Targeted DO NOTHING conflict handling and returned inserted rows; does not itself make the whole create/replay operation atomic.

title: PostgreSQL 16: Transactions
relevantSections: 3.4: transaction block, COMMIT, ROLLBACK and visibility
supports: All-or-nothing transaction boundaries; the three-record create design is an original illustrative application, not executed by this app.

title: PostgreSQL 16: Transaction Isolation
relevantSections: 13.2.1: Read Committed, concurrent conflict visibility and row locks
supports: Statement snapshots, conflicting inserts and locked-row rechecks; product retry deadlines, takedown ordering and replay retention need application design.

title: Cache-Aside pattern
relevantSections: Solution; Problems and considerations: lifetime, consistency and local caching; Workload design
supports: Miss/fill mechanics, stale-data limitations and conditional fallback; the strict mapping/eligibility split and freshness contract are original workshop choices, not an Azure implementation.

title: Timeouts, retries, and backoff with jitter
relevantSections: Failures Happen; Timeouts; Retries and backoff; Jitter
supports: Resource-bounded timeouts, uncertain side effects, retry multiplication and pacing; specific three-layer/three-attempt arithmetic and URL-shortener retry retention are workshop assumptions.
